problem: Visual RL navigation agents overfit when few training scenes exist (e.g. only 8 iGibson scenes), and dynamic-environment tasks (InteractiveNav, SocialNav) have scarce training data. Image augmentations help but combine poorly and transfer badly across simulators.
motivation: Home robots must handle moving people and movable obstacles, but dynamic interactive scene datasets are tiny. The observation is that adding moving pedestrians in training prevents memorizing scene layouts and forces diverse paths, improving generalization even on static tasks.
key_idea: Add several randomly moving pedestrians as dynamic obstacles during RL training (dynamic obstacle augmentation) to improve generalization, optionally combined with Crop/Cutout image augmentation.
insight: Gains from pedestrians are largest with few training scenes (8 or fewer; e.g. +3.5% at 8 scenes vs +0.42% at 72 in PointNav), indicating it mitigates overfitting. Image augmentations (Cutout) are competitive in-domain but degrade under the Gibson-to-iGibson sim-to-sim gap (Table InteractiveNav: Dynamic 61.99 vs Cutout 54.96, Crop 56.11, none 51.00), while Dyn+Crop is best in-domain. Combining Crop+Cutout hurts.
method: Dynamic obstacle augmentation: 3-12 (up to 18 in sweeps) pedestrians, each walking back and forth between two random navigable points >=3 m apart, with speed reduced up to 10% per episode; collision (<0.3 m) terminates the episode.
Image augmentations: Crop (random patch, 8% shorter), Cutout (random black rectangle, scale 0.02-0.33, aspect 0.3-3.33), and Crop&Cutout, applied to depth input.
Policy: ResNet-18 depth encoder + 2-layer LSTM (512) taking goal distance/heading and previous action; outputs Gaussian linear/angular velocity and value; stop is implied by small velocities.
Training: DD-PPO in Habitat, 64 workers on 8 GPUs, 500M steps; reward = -Δgeodesic - 0.002 - 0.02(backward+collision) + 10 success.
Zero-shot sim-to-sim: Habitat-trained agents evaluated directly in iGibson for InteractiveNav without any InteractiveNav-specific reward.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 + 2-layer LSTM (trained from scratch with DD-PPO)
setting.training_data: Gibson-4+ (72 train scenes, subsets of 1-72 scenes, 500M steps RL); challenge agent trained on 8 iGibson scenes imported into Habitat
setting.observation: egocentric depth image + relative goal distance/heading (egomotion) + previous action
setting.action_space: continuous velocity (linear max 0.5 m/s, angular max 90°/s, 10 Hz), stop when velocities are below 10% threshold

numbers_note: Image-augmentation comparison results (Crop/Cutout heatmap) were given only in a figure; full sweep tables for PointNav and SocialNav exist but only representative cells are listed.
results: Dynamic obstacle augmentation improves PointNav and SocialNav success especially with few training scenes (PointNav 8 scenes: 87.89 to 91.41). It is more robust than image augmentation in sim-to-sim InteractiveNav (61.99 vs 51.00 no aug, 56.11 Crop). It won the 2021 iGibson Challenge InteractiveNav track with 31% SR vs 27% for the second place team.
limitations: Challenge success rates are low (~30%) due to small scene layouts, the sim-to-sim gap and frozen furniture in Habitat during training, so agents avoid pushing objects.
InteractiveNav could not be emulated in Habitat, so it is evaluated only zero-shot in iGibson, on training scenes since the challenge set is not public.
Too many pedestrians may make the agent overly conservative; no sim-to-real evaluation and pedestrians are rigid bodies.
